title: Circulation of European literary works
content:
This action will support projects that translate, publish, distribute and promote European literary works written by authors linked to an eligible Creative Europe country by their nationality or place of residence, or recognised as belonging to the European literary heritage.

The action is expected to support around 40 projects, implemented either by a single entity (mono-beneficiary) or by a consortium of organisations (multi-beneficiary).

Along with activities related to literary works, activities that facilitate collaboration between different actors in the book and publishing value chain, such as authors, translators, publishers, distributors, booksellers, libraries, literary events and festivals, can also be funded.

Link to the Funding and Tenders Portal of the EU.

title: European Commission takes the European Heritage Label to the next step of its evolution
content:
The primary purpose of the legal review is to renew and strengthen the action to ensure its continued relevance and impact. This is needed in response to emerging challenges in the implementation of the action and to better align it with the evolving priorities of the EU in the fields of culture and heritage.

Following a stakeholder consultation and evaluation process, the European Commission proposes the following changes to the European Parliament and the Council of the EU for their contribution and approval.

The proposal establishes a European Heritage ‘status’, to be awarded to the selected sites, which will then be inscribed in the ‘European Heritage List’. Sites awarded the Label in the previous decision will automatically receive the status.

The Commission proposal expands the action to include EFTA/EEA countries, candidate countries and potential candidates for EU membership associated to the Creative Europe programme or to subsequent EU programmes supporting culture.

The new legal basis foresees the attribution of a prize to selected and monitored sites awarded upon recommendation of the EHL expert panel.

title: Culture Moves Europe: new call for residency hosts 2026-2027 open
content:
The call provides grants to organisations and individual artists from Creative Europe countries that wish to host international artists and cultural professionals for a residency project. Hosts can invite up to five residents and are expected to provide an appropriate environment, accommodation, workspace and artistic guidance through at least one mentor.

Residency projects should pursue at least two of five objectives:

  • explore
  • create
  • learn
  • connect
  • transform

    • The call is open to projects in the fields of

  • architecture
  • cultural heritage
  • design and fashion design
  • literature
  • music
  • performing arts
  • visual arts

    • Whether you are a non-profit organisation, cultural centre, museum, foundation, company, NGO or self-employed artist, you can apply to become a Culture Moves Europe residency host.

    The call is open until 18 January 2027.

    The call provides financial support to organisations and individual artists that want to host artists and cultural professionals for a residency project. Apply until 18 January 2027.

  • Find out more about the details of the call and how to apply for a residency
